about.heading: About the company
paragraphs: For over 20 years, Barry Smith Electrical Contractors Ltd has been delivering trusted electrical contracting services to domestic, commercial, and industrial clients across Ireland. Built on a reputation for quality workmanship, reliability, and exceptional customer service, we have grown into a respected contractor known for delivering projects safely, on time, and within budget.

We provide a complete range of electrical services, from design and installation through to maintenance and ongoing support. Our experienced team works with homeowners, property developers, architects, engineering consultants, main contractors, and businesses to deliver tailored electrical solutions that meet the highest industry standards.

ev.heading: EV charger installation
ev.intro: We supply and install home electric vehicle chargers across Dublin and Leinster, or install a charger you have already bought. Every installation is carried out by our Safe Electric registered electricians, certified and tested to current Irish wiring standards.
ev.grantBody: Homeowners with off-street parking can claim up to €300 towards the cost of a home charger through the SEAI EV Home Charger Grant. You don't need to own an electric car yet to apply. The grant requires a Safe Electric registered electrician, and we provide the completion certificate and test records you need for your payment claim.

evPage.metaTitle: EV Charger Installation Dublin | Barry Smith Electrical
evPage.metaDescription: Home EV charger supply and installation across Dublin and Leinster by Safe Electric registered electricians. Certified for the SEAI €300 home charger grant.
evPage.heading: EV charger installation in Dublin & Leinster
evPage.lede: Home electric vehicle chargers supplied and installed by Safe Electric registered electricians, certified for the SEAI home charger grant.
grantSteps: Apply online with SEAI. You'll need the MPRN from your electricity bill and your Eircode.
SEAI emails you a Letter of Offer.
We install your charger. The installation must be completed within 6 months of the offer.
We provide the completion certificate and test record sheet. You submit these with your invoice and photos in SEAI's payment request.
SEAI processes payment, which takes approximately 4 to 6 weeks.

faq.question: Do I need to own an electric car to get the grant?
faq.answer: No. SEAI's home charger grant is open to homeowners whether they own an electric vehicle or not.

faq.question: How much is the grant?
faq.answer: Up to €300 towards the purchase and installation of a home charger.

faq.question: Who is eligible?
faq.answer: Homeowners with off-street parking at their property. A property that has already received this grant, or a free ESB ecars charger, is not eligible.

faq.question: Can you install a charger I've already bought?
faq.answer: Yes. We can supply the charger, or install one you have already bought.

faq.question: Which areas do you cover?
faq.answer: We install EV chargers across Dublin and Leinster, including Wicklow.

evPage.sourceNote: Grant details are from SEAI and can change. Check SEAI's website for the current terms before you apply.

faq.question: Do I need a registered electrician to rewire my house?
faq.answer: Yes. The CRU, which regulates electrical contractors in Ireland, says you should always use a Registered Electrical Contractor for electrical work in your home, and that it is the law. Barry Smith Electrical Contractors Ltd is RECI registered.

faq.question: Will I get a completion certificate?
faq.answer: Yes. A Registered Electrical Contractor must give you a Completion Certificate when they do electrical work in your home. It shows the work is safe and up to standard.

faq.question: Do you upgrade fuse boards?
faq.answer: Yes. We carry out fuse board upgrades and replacements.

faq.question: Do you do the electrical work for extensions and renovations?
faq.answer: Yes. We carry out electrical work for extensions and renovations as well as house rewires.

faq.question: Which areas do you cover?
faq.answer: We work across Dublin and Leinster, including Wicklow.

servicePages.sourceNote: Information on Registered Electrical Contractors and completion certificates is from the Commission for Regulation of Utilities (CRU).

faq.question: What standard applies to fire alarm systems in Ireland?
faq.answer: The current Irish Standard is I.S. 3218:2024, published by the NSAI. It gives guidelines for the planning, design, installation, commissioning, servicing and maintenance of fire detection and fire alarm systems, including in residential and domestic premises.
